questions.question: Why does semantic HTML matter — name the key elements and their rules?
questions.title: Html Semantic Basics
questions.direct_answer: Semantic elements declare MEANING (header, nav, main, article, section, aside, footer) that browsers, screen readers, and search engines can act on — instead of div/span soup that says nothing. Rules: exactly one <main> per page; <article> = independently distributable content; <section> = thematic group with a heading; <div> = last resort. Benefits: free accessibility landmarks, better SEO understanding, keyboard focus behavior, and code that reads like its structure.

    S --> SEO[crawlers understand structure]
